subject: Taxes
title: Ireland's Tax Magic
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Ireland's Tax Magic.

hook.text: Ireland's 12.5% corporate tax rate attracted Apple, Google, and Facebook.

buildup.text: The 'Double Irish' arrangement let companies route profits through two Irish entities.

discovery.text: Apple paid an effective tax rate of 0.005% in Ireland in 2014.

twist.text: The EU ordered Apple to repay €13 billion in back taxes to Ireland. Ireland fought the ruling—it didn't want the money.

climax.text: Ireland chose corporate investment over tax revenue. Low rates attracted jobs—300,000 work for multinationals there.

punchline.text: 0.005% tax on Apple. Ireland fought to keep it that way.

quiz.question: Why did Ireland fight an EU order to collect €13 billion from Apple?
options: It valued attracting multinationals more than one-time revenue
